observed.facings.png: Three facings on a checkerboard at one shared scale. South is a squat, wide four-legged beast seen from the front. Its head is small and low between thick pillar legs, and a ridge of plates runs up the back. East is a long side profile: a domed armoured back with a row of upright plates along the spine, a short stubby tail on the left and a small blunt head on the right. North shows the rump with a ringed, cone-shaped tail hanging down and no face. Every facing is covered in irregular grey-brown stone plates, with orange-glowing cracks between some of them. All three facings look about the same height.
observed.south.png: Front view of a heavy quadruped built from rough stone slabs. A small, scowling, stony face with brow ridges and tiny eyes sits low at the centre, under a dome of overlapping plates with a ridge of spikes along the top. Glowing orange seams show at the shoulders. Four thick, segmented pillar legs end in blocky stone feet. Clean transparent background, no shadow.
observed.east.png: Side profile facing right. The body is long and barrel-shaped, made of banded stone plates, with a dorsal row of upright flat plates. Bright orange molten seams run between plates along the flank and at the shoulder and hip. The head is small and low with a beaked snout and a small eye. The tail is short, blunt and plated, at the left. The sprite runs almost the full canvas width (alpha x 5 to 1020) but does not touch either edge. A few reddish fringe pixels sit along the top plate edges.
observed.north.png: Rear view: the back of the plated dome, the dorsal spikes seen end-on at the top, and a segmented conical tail hanging down the middle. Glowing seams show where the tail meets the haunches. The hind legs are pillar-like with stone feet. No face and no eyes. Clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom, a crop of the beast's flank (stone plates, lava seams, crisp detail) next to the vanilla human, who stands far smaller than the visible section of the body. At normal play (32 px per cell), the whole beast in side view is about 7 cells long beside a human and a rat about 1 cell tall. It reads as a huge plated stone creature with an orange glow at the seams.

SIGNATURE.seen: The banded mineral hide with seams glowing between the plates is the most visible thing on every facing, strongest on east.

ALIEN.seen: Reads first as a stone, lava-veined beast. The ankylosaur or tortoise body plan is there, but the mineral plates and glowing seams carry the identity. It does not read as a recoloured Earth animal.

DEPARTURES.seen: 1. Banded hide of mineral, not skin or fur: PRESENT. The whole body is stone slabs in bands, with molten seams between them.

STYLE.seen: Realistic stone texture with naturalistic lighting, not cute or cel-shaded. It leans toward a crisp 3D-render look rather than painterly, and the scowling face is a little golem-like, but neither is cartoonish.

OURS.seen: Bespoke generated creature matching the description; no vanilla or other-mod donor recognisable.

ALPHA.seen: Transparent background on all three facings, with no ground patch or shadow. Only about 6 stray reddish fringe pixels on the east top edge, negligible.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: At normal play it is about 7 cells long against a 1-cell human and dwarfs everything: a true giant, as the note requires.

SCALE.seen: Megafauna-sized beside the human, which fits 'migratory megafauna'.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px per cell it reads as a big plated grey-brown mass with orange seam accents, a clear silhouette with legs, and separates from the ground.

The south face has small, deeply recessed eyes, irregular fractured brows and a closed, heavy muzzle. Its stern expression is visible, but the eyes lack glossy enlargement and the face retains the same rough mineral treatment as the body; it does not clearly read as cute or cartoonish.

request.subject: RM_FurnaceBeast

edits.change: The hide is painted in loose, visible brushwork in the manner of vanilla RimWorld animals: plates are irregular value shapes of very different sizes, some large flat slabs, some small chips, with simple two- or three-tone shading, soft hand-painted edges, and only a few selective details. The finish is flat gouache-like colour blocks with a clean dark outline, readable at small gameplay scale.

The body plan is alien and tall-legged: a long, high-shouldered migratory walker standing on four long, columnar, jointed legs with the belly raised well above the ground, a narrow deep ribcage-like kiln barrel body, and a long, low, forward-reaching neck ending in a broad, flat, wedge-shaped plated head with a wide scoop-like grazing mouth (a shovel-shaped muzzle for stripping thornvine). The back is a tapering ridge of stacked mineral bands rather than a domed shell.

The silhouette alone reads as alien: stacked horizontal mineral bands stepping down the flank like terraced strata, a heat-vent chimney of plates rising over the shoulders, a long whip-like banded tail ending in a stone club. No armoured dorsal row, no dome.

The east view is framed small within the canvas: the whole animal, from the tail tip to the muzzle tip, occupies about 80 percent of the canvas width, with clear transparent margin of at least 10 percent on the left and right, above the back ridge and below the feet.

invariants: banded mineral hide of cool grey, tan and ochre stone, not skin or fur
glowing ember orange-yellow seams between plates, brightest at shoulder, flank and haunch, dimmer deep red elsewhere
plates stay cool stone; the only strong orange is the heat in the seams
colossal scale, exactly four legs, feet on one ground line
tiny dark deep-set eyes under a heavy plated brow
transparent background, clean dark outline, painterly vanilla RimWorld style
north view is the rear (back, tail and haunches, eyes hidden), south view is the front, same body height as east
request.prompt: A realistic, painterly vanilla RimWorld-style sprite of the furnace-beast, a colossal migratory megafauna and the largest animal on its world, an alien walking kiln of banded mineral, on a transparent background with a clean dark outline. The body plan is alien and tall-legged: a long, high-shouldered walker standing on exactly four long, thick, columnar legs with the belly raised well above the ground and broad flat round feet, one leg at each corner. The torso is a deep, narrow, kiln-like barrel whose flank is built of stacked horizontal mineral bands stepping down like terraced strata. A tapering ridge of stacked mineral bands, with a chimney-like cluster of plates rising over the shoulders, forms the back, not a domed shell and not an armoured dorsal row. A long, low neck reaches forward and ends in a broad, flat, wedge-shaped plated head with a wide scoop-like grazing mouth, a shovel-shaped muzzle made for stripping thornvine. The tiny dark deep-set eyes sit beneath a heavy plated brow. A long, whip-like banded tail ends in a stone club. The hide is mineral, not skin or fur: banded strata of cool grey, tan and ochre stone, built from irregular plates of very different sizes, some large flat slabs and some small chips. It is painted in loose, visible brushwork in the manner of vanilla RimWorld animals: simple two- or three-tone value shapes, flat gouache-like colour blocks, soft hand-painted plate edges, and only a few selective details such as a dusting of grey ash on the upper surfaces and a few fine cracks. The cracks and seams between the plates glow a warm ember orange-yellow like coals showing through gaps in a stove: narrow lines with a gentle inner light, bright yellow-orange at a few joints (shoulder, flank, haunch) and dimmer deep red elsewhere, so the beast reads as hot inside at a glance while the plates themselves stay cool stone. The underbelly shows smaller interlocking stone plates with glowing seams. The sprite reads clearly at small gameplay scale, with a clean dark silhouette and crisp plate edges against a fully transparent background, with opaque pixels right up to the dark outline and nothing floating outside it. The animal has exactly four legs. It is drawn at one fixed scale in every view: the north view shows the rear, seen from behind, with back, tail and haunches and the eyes hidden, drawn at the same body height as the east view; the south view shows the front, with eyes toward the viewer, drawn at the same body height as the east view; and in every view the feet rest on the same ground line. The east side view frames the complete animal, from tail tip to muzzle tip, within about 80 percent of the canvas width, with at least 10 percent clear transparent margin on the left and right and above and below, and every foot complete inside the canvas.
